english.title: Registered early years provider fail to ensure person caring for a child did not use corporal punishment
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being a registered early years provider under the Childcare Act 2006 failed, without reasonable excuse, to comply with the requirements of regulation 7(1) of the Early Years Foundation Stage (Welfare Requirements) Regulations 2012 to ensure as far as was reasonably practicable that corporal punishment was not used by a person who

(A)_[cared for]_
(B)_[was in regular contact with]_

children for whom early years provision was being provided
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 7(1)(a) and 12(1) of the Early Years Foundation Stage (Welfare Requirements) Regulations 2012.

english.notes:
(i) Regulation 7(2) of the Early Years Foundation Stage (Welfare Requirements) Regulations 2012 provides that a person will not be taken to have used corporal punishment if the action was taken for reasons that include averting an immediate danger of personal injury to, or an immediate danger of death of, any person including the child.
(ii) Regulation 7(3) of the Early Years Foundation Stage (Welfare Requirements) Regulations 2012 provides that "corporal punishment" means anything done for the purposes of punishing the child (whether or not there are other reasons for doing it) which, absent any justification, would constitute battery.
(iii) Regulation 12 of the Early Years Foundation Stage (Welfare Requirements) Regulations 2012 specifies proceedings for proceedings in respect of this offence may only be taken by (a) the Chief Inspector and (b) after the Chief Inspector has allowed a period not exceeding one month, beginning with the date the Chief Inspector notified the registered early years provider of the decision to take proceedings, for the registered early years provider to make representations.
(iv) Section 98 of the Childcare Act 2006 defines "the Chief Inspector" as His Majesty's Chief Inspector of Schools in England.
(v) Section 10 of the Interpretation Act 1978 states that any reference to the Sovereign reigning at the time of the passing of the Act is to be construed, unless the contrary intention appears, as a reference to the Sovereign for the time being. As such, references to ‘Her Majesty’ and ‘the Queen’ have been replaced in the wording of the notes above to state ‘His Majesty’ or ‘the King’, although this may not be the strict wording of the legislation.
